name: grep_files
description: Alias of search_files using familiar grep/rg terminology. Search plain-text files by content inside registered source directories with literal matching by default, plus opt-in Rust regex matching. Prefer literal mode for exact user text, identifiers, snippets, and strings containing regex metacharacters such as |, ., *, ?, [, or (. Set regex=true only when the query is intentionally a regex; escape metacharacters such as \| only in regex mode when they should be matched literally. Supports include/exclude globs, hidden-file control, line numbers, and optional context lines. Prefer this for coding/codebase browsing and whenever the user asks to grep, rg, or find text inside local files. Use it before read_file/read_files unless an exact file or path is already known.

query.description: Text to search for. Treated as exact literal text unless regex=true, so characters such as | are literal by default.

path.description: Optional file or directory path to search. If omitted, searches all directories in the current source scope.

regex.description: Treat query as a Rust regular expression instead of literal text (default false). Do not enable this for exact text; if regex=true and you need a literal |, escape it as \|.

include_globs.description: Optional glob patterns to include, such as *.md or notes/**/*.txt

exclude_globs.description: Optional glob patterns to exclude, such as **/archive/**

max_results.description: Maximum number of matching lines to return (default 50, max 200)

context_lines.description: Number of surrounding lines to include before and after each match (default 0, max 3)

include_hidden.description: Include dotfiles and hidden directories (default false)
